recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It is a narrow, in-build documentation fix completing the published non-substantive link request without changing conformance rules or duplicating workflow guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-11478 is a Published/Persuasive Pharmacy change request from the DSTU2 ballot asking the medications module to have a hyperlink to Workflow and probably Administration; the resolution was to agree and review the module with links.
initial_application: No medication-module commit explicitly tagged FHIR-11478 was found. Historical source showed Workflow links were already present from July 2016 medication module work, and the October 2016 @9953 commit applied adjacent medication-module issues FHIR-11479 and FHIR-11481 without adding an Administration module link.
additional_context: The current build hierarchy includes Medications, Administration, and Workflow module pages. The medications module already linked to Workflow from MedicationRequest, Common Use Cases, and Other resources, but had no administration-module.html link before this reconciliation. Zulip and Confluence searches found no issue-key record that narrowed or reversed the Jira request.
reconciliation: Added one Administration Module link in source/medications-module.html's Other resources section, pointing medication readers to foundational Patient, Practitioner, Organization, Encounter, and Location context used by medication records. No other source was changed because existing Workflow links already satisfy that part of the issue.
